cohort: The study included 224 gravid singleton women meeting inclusion criteria at a tertiary care centre.
finding: Maternal obesity is strongly associated with increased rates of gestational diabetes, hypertension, intrahepatic cholestasis, caesarean delivery, maternal wound infections, shoulder dystocia, preterm birth, higher neonatal birth weights, lower APGAR scores, and greater NICU admissions.
mod_finding: Caesarean section (LSCS) was significantly more frequent in obese women (77.9%) compared to non-obese women (54.6%).
